false_positives.evidence: MemoryModel.findAll({ include: [UserModel] }) returned in res.json; route registered at server.ts:670 with no isAuthorized
false_positives.fix: Require authentication, and restrict the included User to non-sensitive attributes (e.g. attributes: ['id','username']).
false_positives.title: Unauthenticated /rest/memories returns joined user records incl. password hashes

trace.note: include: [UserModel] with all attributes serialized to the response

false_positives.why: GET /rest/memories needs no authentication and eager-loads the full UserModel (email, MD5 password hash, role, totpSecret, deluxeToken) for every memory owner, with no attribute exclusion.

false_positives.evidence: expressJwt({ secret: publicKey }); jws.verify(token, publicKey); jwt.verify(token, publicKey, cb) at line 189 - no algorithms option
false_positives.fix: Pass algorithms: ['RS256'] to every verify call, and upgrade jsonwebtoken and express-jwt to maintained versions.
false_positives.title: JWT verification does not pin the algorithm (RS256 to HS256 confusion)

trace.note: Authorization bearer token controlled by client
verification with public key and no algorithm restriction

false_positives.why: Verification takes the algorithm from the token header and passes the RSA public key as the secret. The public key is downloadable from /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub, so an attacker can sign an HS256 token using it as an HMAC secret and be accepted as any user or role. Based on the pinned old library versions; library internals were not inspected (no node_modules).

false_positives.evidence: req.body.password === '<redacted>' compared for admin@, support@, mc.safesearch@, amy@, J12934@, testing@ and a gmail account
false_positives.fix: Delete the credential literals from application code and seed accounts with random or runtime-injected passwords.
false_positives.title: Real account credentials hard-coded in login handler
false_positives.why: Plaintext passwords for seeded privileged and customer accounts (including admin, with a trivially weak password) are embedded in source. They are reachable credentials for the seeded accounts, so anyone with the code can log in.

false_positives.evidence: app.post('/rest/user/login', login()) with no rateLimit middleware (limiters exist only for reset-password and 2FA)
false_positives.fix: Add per-account and per-IP rate limiting (keyed on a server-derived IP) with lockout or backoff.
false_positives.title: No attempt limit on login
false_positives.why: Credentials can be guessed or sprayed against the login endpoint without throttling. Passwords are unsalted MD5 and seeded accounts have weak passwords.

false_positives.evidence: res.json({ config: structuredClone(config.util.toObject(config)) }) at /rest/admin/application-configuration, registered at server.ts:646 without authorization
false_positives.fix: Require admin authorization and return only the public-facing settings the client needs.
false_positives.title: Unauthenticated admin application-configuration endpoint
false_positives.why: The full server configuration (minus one field) is returned to anyone; the /rest/admin path is not protected. Contents of config files were not in scope, so severity depends on what they hold.

false_positives.evidence: generateCoupon: z85.encode(toMMMYY(date) + '-' + discount); discountFromCoupon decodes and accepts any correctly formatted current-month value
false_positives.fix: Issue random coupon codes stored server-side, or sign them with an HMAC and verify it.
false_positives.title: Discount coupons are forgeable (encoding, not a signature)
false_positives.why: z85 is a public reversible encoding with no secret or MAC, so any user can mint a coupon for the current month with an arbitrary discount (two digits) and apply it at /rest/basket/:id/coupon/:coupon.

false_positives.fix: Upgrade to a current express-jwt and set algorithms explicitly.
false_positives.title: express-jwt 0.1.3 is an obsolete release with a known authorization-bypass advisory
false_positives.why: express-jwt below 6.0.0 is affected by CVE-2020-15084 (authorization bypass when algorithms is not specified). This is matched from widely reported advisory knowledge, not repository metadata.

false_positives.fix: Upgrade to a maintained sanitize-html release.
false_positives.title: sanitize-html 1.4.2 is an obsolete release with a known XSS advisory
false_positives.why: Versions before 1.4.3 are affected by CVE-2016-1000237 (XSS via crafted input), and the library is the project's HTML sanitizer for usernames and emails. This is matched from widely reported advisory knowledge, not repository metadata.

false_positives.fix: Load the key at runtime from a secret manager; use a salted slow hash for answers.
false_positives.title: Hard-coded HMAC key protecting security-question answers
false_positives.why: Security answers are stored as HMACs with a key that is in the source, so a leaked database can be brute-forced offline against a common-answer list. A second literal secret is the cookie-parser secret at server.ts:321.

false_positives.evidence: WalletModel.increment({ balance: req.body.balance }, { where: { UserId: req.body.UserId } })
false_positives.fix: Charge the card through a payment provider first; validate the amount as a positive bounded number.
false_positives.title: Wallet top-up credits an arbitrary client-supplied amount
false_positives.why: The credited amount comes from the body and no charge is made against the card, which is only checked for existence. A user can add any balance, then spend it on orders or deluxe membership.
